name: Forty-Five
description: Forty-Five (45s) is a traditional trick-taking game with Irish roots, most famously played in Ireland and Atlantic Canada (New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, and Newfoundland). A simplified descendant of 'Spoil Five', the game is known for its idiosyncratic card rankings, where the 5 of trumps is the ultimate card and the Ace of Hearts is permanently the third-highest trump regardless of the suit led. The name comes from the target score of 45 points, achieved across several rounds of five-trick hands.

content.text: Forty-Five (45s) is a traditional trick-taking game with Irish roots, most famously played in Ireland and Atlantic Canada (New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, and Newfoundland). A simplified descendant of 'Spoil Five', the game is known for its idiosyncratic card rankings, where the 5 of trumps is the ultimate card and the Ace of Hearts is permanently the third-highest trump regardless of the suit led. The name comes from the target score of 45 points, achieved across several rounds of five-trick hands.

Forty-Five is a streamlined version of the ancient Irish game 'Spoil Five,' which was described as the national game of Ireland as early as the 18th century. It traveled with Irish immigrants to the Maritimes of Canada and the New England states, where it remains a cultural identifier.
4 players (2 vs 2) is the standard partnership format. Can be played 2, 3, or 6ndhanded.
Each player is dealt 5 cards (traditionally 3 then 2, or 2 then 3). The next card is turned up to determine the trump suit.
